title.zh: 卷八十六 志第六十二 河渠四
title.raw: 卷八十六 志第六十二 河渠四 Volume 86 Treatises 62: Rivers and Canals 4

sentences.zh: 運河下 海運

translations.literal: Grand Canal, Part Two; Sea Transport
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal (continued); Sea Transport

sentences.zh: 江南運河，自杭州北郭務至謝村北，為十二里洋，為塘棲，德清之水入之。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan Grand Canal, from Beiguo Post north of Hangzhou to the north of Xiecun, forms the Twelve-li Ocean, forms Tangqi, and the waters of Deqing enter it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan stretch of the Grand Canal runs from Beiguo Post north of Hangzhou to the north of Xiecun, passing through the Twelve-li Ocean and Tangqi, into which the waters of Deqing flow.

sentences.zh: 逾北陸橋入崇德界，過松老抵高新橋，海鹽支河通之。

translations.literal: Crossing Beilu Bridge it enters the border of Chongde, passes Songlao and reaches Gaoxin Bridge, and the Haiyan branch canal connects with it.
translations.idiomatic: It crosses Beilu Bridge into Chongde territory, passes Songlao to reach Gaoxin Bridge, where the Haiyan branch canal joins it.

sentences.zh: 繞崇德城南，轉東北，至小高陽橋東，過石門塘，折而東，為王灣。

translations.literal: It circles south of Chongde city, turns northeast to east of Xiaogaoyang Bridge, passes Shimen Pond, turns east, and becomes Wang Bay.
translations.idiomatic: Skirting the south of Chongde city, it turns northeast to the east of Xiaogaoyang Bridge, crosses Shimen Pond, bends eastward, and forms Wang Bay.

sentences.zh: 至皁林，水深者及丈。

translations.literal: Reaching Zaolin, where the water is deep it reaches a zhang.
translations.idiomatic: At Zaolin the depth of the channel reaches as much as ten feet in places.

sentences.zh: 過永新，入秀水界，逾陡門鎮，北為分鄉鋪，稍東為繡塔。

translations.literal: Passing Yongxin, it enters Xiushui territory, crosses Doumen Town; to the north is Fenxiang Post, and slightly east is Xiuta.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Yongxin it enters Xiushui, crosses Doumen Town, with Fenxiang Post to the north and Xiuta a little to the east.

sentences.zh: 北由嘉興城西轉而北，出杉青三閘，至王江涇鎮，松江運艘自東來會之。

translations.literal: Northward from west of Jiaxing city it turns north, exits the three Shaqing sluices, reaches Wangjiangjing Town, and grain transports from Songjiang join it from the east.
translations.idiomatic: North of Jiaxing it swings west of the city and then north, passes the three Shaqing sluices to Wangjiangjing, where grain barges from Songjiang converge from the east.

sentences.zh: 北為平望驛，東通鶯脰湖，湖州運艘自西出新興橋會之。

translations.literal: To the north is Pingwang Post; east it connects to Yingdou Lake, and grain transports from Huzhou join it from the west at Xinxing Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Farther north lies Pingwang Post; to the east it opens on Yingdou Lake, and Huzhou grain barges meet it from the west at Xinxing Bridge.

sentences.zh: 北至松陵驛，由吳江至三里橋，北有震澤，南有黃天蕩，水勢澎湃，夾浦橋屢建。

translations.literal: North to Songling Post, from Wujiang to Sanli Bridge; to the north is Zhenze, to the south Huangtiandang; the water is surging, and Jiapu Bridge has been built repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: It runs north to Songling Post and from Wujiang to Sanli Bridge, with Zhenze to the north and Huangtiandang to the south; the current runs fierce here, and Jiapu Bridge has had to be rebuilt again and again.

sentences.zh: 北經蘇州城東鯰魚口，水由□□塘入之。

translations.literal: Northward it passes Catfish Mouth east of Suzhou city, and water enters through the □□ pond canal.
translations.idiomatic: It continues north past Catfish Mouth east of Suzhou, where water feeds in from the Hengtang canal.

sentences.zh: 北至楓橋，由射瀆經滸墅□關，過白鶴鋪，長洲、無錫兩邑之界也。

translations.literal: North to Maple Bridge, by Shedu through Huxu □ Pass, past Baihe Post—the boundary of Changzhou and Wuxi two districts.
translations.idiomatic: It reaches Maple Bridge, follows the Shedu channel through Huxu Pass, passes Baihe Post, and marks the border between Changzhou and Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 錫山驛水僅浮瓦礫。

translations.literal: At Xishan Post the water barely floats tile rubble.
translations.idiomatic: At Xishan Post the water is so shallow that it barely floats broken tiles.

sentences.zh: 過黃埠，至洛社橋，江陰九里河之水通之。

translations.literal: Passing Huangbu, reaching Luoshe Bridge, the waters of Jiangyin's Nine-li River connect with it.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Huangbu it comes to Luoshe Bridge, where the Nine-li River of Jiangyin joins the canal.

sentences.zh: 西北為常州，漕河舊貫城，入東水門，由西水門出。

translations.literal: Northwest is Changzhou; the grain canal formerly ran through the city, entering the East Water Gate and exiting the West Water Gate.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest lies Changzhou, where the grain canal once ran straight through the city, entering by the East Water Gate and leaving by the West Water Gate.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末防倭，改從南城壕。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiajing reign, to guard against Wokou raids, it was changed to follow the south city moat.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jiajing reign, as a defense against Japanese pirates, the route was shifted to the south city moat.

sentences.zh: 江陰，順塘河水由城東通丁堰，沙子湖在其西南，宜興鐘溪之水入之。

translations.literal: At Jiangyin, Shuntang River water from east of the city connects to Dingyan; Shazi Lake is southwest of it, and the waters of Yixing's Zhongxi enter it.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangyin the Shuntang River flows from east of the city to Dingyan; Shazi Lake lies to the southwest, fed by the Zhongxi stream from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 又西，直瀆水入之，又西為奔牛、呂城二閘，常、鎮界其中，皆有月河以佐節宣，後並廢。

translations.literal: Farther west, Zhidu water enters it; farther west are the two sluices of Benniu and Lücheng, with the Changzhou–Zhenjiang border between them; each had a moon canal to assist regulation and discharge, and later all were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Still farther west the Zhidu channel feeds in; beyond that stand the Benniu and Lücheng sluices on the Changzhou–Zhenjiang border, each once paired with a relief canal for flow control, though these were later abandoned.

sentences.zh: 其南為金壇河，溧陽、高淳之水出焉。

translations.literal: To its south is the Jintan River, from which the waters of Liyang and Gaochun issue.
translations.idiomatic: South of this stretch runs the Jintan River, carrying the waters of Liyang and Gaochun.

sentences.zh: 丹陽南二十里為陵口，北二十五里為黃泥壩，舊皆置閘。

translations.literal: Twenty li south of Danyang is Lingkou, twenty-five li north is Huangniba; sluices were formerly placed at both.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li south of Danyang stands Lingkou, and twenty-five li north Huangniba; sluices once stood at each.

sentences.zh: 練湖水高漕河數丈，一由三思橋，一由仁智橋，皆入運。

translations.literal: Lianhu Lake's water is several zhang higher than the grain canal; one [channel] by Sansi Bridge, one by Renzhi Bridge—both enter the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The water of Lianhu Lake stands several zhang above the grain canal; one outlet runs through Sansi Bridge and another through Renzhi Bridge, both feeding the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 北過丹徒鎮有豬婆灘，多軟沙。

translations.literal: North past Dantu Town is Zhupoba, with much soft sand.
translations.idiomatic: North of Dantu Town lies Zhupoba, notorious for soft sandbanks.

sentences.zh: 丹徒以上運道，視江潮為盈涸。

translations.literal: Above Dantu the transport channel's fullness or dryness depends on the Yangtze tides.
translations.idiomatic: Upstream of Dantu the transport channel rises and falls with the Yangtze tides.

sentences.zh: 過鎮江，出京口閘，閘外沙堵延袤二十丈，可藏舟避風，由此浮於江，與瓜步對。

translations.literal: Passing Zhenjiang, exiting Jingkou Sluice; outside the sluice a sand embankment extends twenty zhang, where boats can be hidden to avoid wind; from here they float on the river, opposite Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: The route passes Zhenjiang and leaves by Jingkou Sluice; outside the sluice a sand bar twenty zhang long shelters boats from wind, and from there craft enter the Yangtze opposite Guabu.

sentences.zh: 自北郭至京口首尾八百餘里，皆平流。

translations.literal: From Beiguo to Jingkou, head to tail more than eight hundred li, all level current.
translations.idiomatic: From Beiguo to Jingkou the full run of more than eight hundred li is level water throughout.

sentences.zh: 曆嘉而蘇，眾水所聚，至常州以西，地漸高仰，水淺易泄，盈涸不恆，時浚時壅，往往兼取孟瀆、德勝兩河，東浮大江，以達揚泰。

translations.literal: Passing Jiaxing and Suzhou, where many waters gather, west of Changzhou the land gradually rises, the water is shallow and easily drains, fullness and dryness are not constant, dredged at times and silted at times; often both the Mengdu and Desheng rivers are used, floating east on the Great River to reach Yangzhou and Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through Jiaxing and Suzhou, where countless streams converge, the land west of Changzhou gradually climbs; the channel grows shallow, drains easily, and alternates between flood and drought. Dredging and silting follow one another in turn, and transport often relies on the Mengdu and Desheng rivers as well, sending boats east on the Yangtze to reach Yangzhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年嘗命崇山侯李新開溧水胭脂河，以通浙漕，免丹陽輸挽及大江風濤之險。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu the emperor once ordered Chongshan Marquis Li Xin to open the Lishui Yanzhi River, to connect Zhejiang grain transport, avoiding the hauling at Danyang and the dangers of wind and waves on the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 26 the court once ordered Chongshan Marquis Li Xin to cut the Yanzhi River at Lishui so Zhejiang grain could reach the capital without the overland haul at Danyang or the perils of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 而三吳之粟，必由常、鎮。

translations.literal: Yet the grain of the Three Wu must pass through Changzhou and Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, grain from the Three Wu had to go by way of Changzhou and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 三十一年浚奔牛、呂城二壩河道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the Benniu and Lücheng two-dam river channel was dredged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 the channel at the Benniu and Lücheng dams was dredged.

sentences.zh: 永樂間，修練湖堤。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign, the Lianhu Lake dikes were repaired.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign the dikes of Lianhu Lake were repaired.

sentences.zh: 即命通政張璉發民丁十萬，浚常州孟瀆河，又浚蘭陵溝，北至孟瀆河閘，六千餘丈，南至奔牛鎮，千二百餘丈。

translations.literal: He then ordered Commissioner of Transmission Zhang Lian to mobilize one hundred thousand corvée laborers to dredge Changzhou's Mengdu River, and also dredge Lanling Ditch—north to the Mengdu River sluice more than six thousand zhang, south to Benniu Town more than one thousand two hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Commissioner of Transmission Zhang Lian to call up one hundred thousand laborers to dredge the Mengdu River at Changzhou and the Lanling Ditch as well—more than six thousand zhang north to the Mengdu sluice and more than twelve hundred zhang south to Benniu Town.

sentences.zh: 已，復浚鎮江京口、新港及甘露三港，以達於江。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again dredged Zhenjiang's Jingkou, Xingang, and the three Ganlu harbors, to reach the river.
translations.idiomatic: After that Jingkou, Xingang, and the three Ganlu harbors at Zhenjiang were dredged again to open a path to the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 漕舟自奔牛溯京口，水涸則改從孟瀆右趨瓜洲，抵白塔，以為常。

translations.literal: Grain transports from Benniu went upstream to Jingkou; when the water dried they changed to the right of Mengdu toward Guazhou, reaching Baita, as the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Grain barges from Benniu went upstream toward Jingkou; when the channel ran low they turned east on the Mengdu branch to Guazhou and Baita, which became the usual route.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年從武進民請，疏德勝新河四十里。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuande, following a petition from the people of Wujin, the new Desheng River was opened for forty li.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 6, at the request of the people of Wujin, the new Desheng River was cut for forty li.

sentences.zh: 八年，工竣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The work was finished in year 8.

sentences.zh: 漕舟自德勝北入江，直泰興之北新河。

translations.literal: Grain transports from Desheng entered the river northward, straight to Taixing's Beixin River.
translations.idiomatic: Grain barges left Desheng north into the Yangtze and ran straight to Taixing's Beixin River.

sentences.zh: 由泰州壩抵揚子灣入漕河，視白塔尤便。

translations.literal: From Taizhou Dam reaching Yangzi Bay to enter the grain canal was even more convenient than Baita.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taizhou dam to Yangzi Bay and into the grain canal was even handier than the Baita route.

sentences.zh: 於是漕河及孟瀆、德勝三河並通，皆可濟運矣。

translations.literal: Thus the grain canal and the Mengdu and Desheng three rivers were all connected, and all could aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: The grain canal and the Mengdu and Desheng branches were now all open, and any of them could serve transport.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，廷臣上言：「自新港至奔牛，漕河百五十里，舊有水車卷江潮灌注，通舟溉田。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, a court official memorialized: "From Xingang to Benniu, the grain canal one hundred fifty li—formerly there were water wheels lifting Yangtze tides to pour in, for passing boats and irrigating fields.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 1 a court official reported: "From Xingang to Benniu the grain canal runs one hundred fifty li. Water wheels once lifted Yangtze water into it for navigation and irrigation.

sentences.zh: 請支官錢置車。

translations.literal: We request disbursing official funds to install the wheels."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that official funds be spent to restore them."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 然三河之入江口，皆自卑而高，其水亦更迭盈縮。

translations.literal: Yet where the three rivers enter the Yangtze mouth, all are from low to high, and their waters also alternately rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all three outlets enter the Yangtze from lower to higher ground, and their levels rose and fell by turns.

sentences.zh: 八年，武進民請浚德勝及北新河。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the people of Wujin requested dredging Desheng and the Beixin River.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the people of Wujin asked that Desheng and the Beixin River be dredged.

sentences.zh: 浙江都司蕭華則請浚孟瀆。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Regional Commander Xiao Hua then requested dredging Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Regional Commander Xiao Hua asked that Mengdu be dredged.

sentences.zh: 巡撫周忱定議浚兩河，而罷北新築壩。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen decided to dredge the two rivers and abandon building a dam on Beixin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen decided to dredge both rivers and drop the plan to dam the Beixin.

sentences.zh: 白塔河之大橋閘以時啟閉，而常、鎮漕河亦疏浚焉。

translations.literal: The Great Bridge Sluice on the Baita River was opened and closed according to season, and the Changzhou–Zhenjiang grain canal was also dredged.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Bridge Sluice on the Baita River was opened and closed on schedule, and the grain canal through Changzhou and Zhenjiang was dredged as well.

sentences.zh: 景泰間，漕河復淤，遂引漕舟盡由孟瀆。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign the grain canal silted up again, and grain transports were all directed through Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign the grain canal silted up again, and all grain traffic was sent through Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 三年，御史練綱言：「漕舟從夏港及孟瀆出江，逆行三百里，始達瓜洲。

translations.literal: In the third year Censor Lian Gang said: "Grain transports from Xiagang and Mengdu exit the river, going against the current three hundred li before reaching Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Censor Lian Gang said: "Barges leaving by Xiagang and Mengdu must buck the current three hundred li before they reach Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 德勝直北新，而白塔又與孟瀆斜直，由此兩岸橫渡甚近，宜大疏淤塞。

translations.literal: Desheng goes straight to Beixin, while Baita is also oblique to Mengdu; from these two shores the cross passage is very close—great dredging of silt blockage should be done."
translations.idiomatic: Desheng runs straight to Beixin, and Baita lies on a diagonal to Mengdu, so the crossing between the two banks is very short. The silt should be cleared on a large scale."

sentences.zh: 」帝命尚書石璞措置。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister Shi Pu to arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Minister Shi Pu to take charge.

sentences.zh: 會有請鑿鎮江七里港，引金山上流通丹陽，以避孟瀆險者。

translations.literal: Just then there was a request to cut Zhenjiang's Qili Harbor, drawing Jinshan upper waters to flow through Danyang, to avoid Mengdu's dangers.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time some proposed cutting Qili Harbor at Zhenjiang to draw water from above Jinshan through Danyang and avoid the hazards of Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 鎮江知府林鶚以為迂道多石，壞民田墓多，宜浚京口閘、甘露壩，道里近，功力省。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang Prefect Lin E held that the detour had much rock, damaged much commoners' fields and tombs, and that Jingkou Sluice and Ganlu Dam should be dredged—the route was nearer and the labor lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang Prefect Lin E argued that the detour was rocky, would ruin too much farmland and graves, and that dredging Jingkou Sluice and Ganlu Dam would be shorter and cheaper.

sentences.zh: 乃從鶚議。

translations.literal: They followed E's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed Lin E's advice.

sentences.zh: 浙江參政胡清又欲去新港、奔牛等壩，置石閘以蓄泉。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Qing also wished to remove the Xingang, Benniu, and other dams and set stone sluices to store spring water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Vice Commissioner Hu Qing also wanted the dams at Xingang and Benniu removed and stone sluices built to hold back the water.

sentences.zh: 亦從其請。

translations.literal: That request was also granted.
translations.idiomatic: That too was approved.

sentences.zh: 而浚德勝河與鑿港之議俱寢。

translations.literal: Yet the proposals to dredge Desheng River and cut the harbor were both shelved.
translations.idiomatic: But the plans to dredge Desheng and cut the new harbor were both dropped.

sentences.zh: 然石閘雖建，蓄水不能多，漕舟仍入孟瀆。

translations.literal: Yet though the stone sluices were built, they could not store much water, and grain transports still entered Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Though the stone sluices were built, they could hold little water, and grain barges still used Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，尚寶少卿淩信言，糧艘從鎮江裏河為便。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun, Court of Imperial Entertainments Junior Companion Ling Xin said that grain ships via Zhenjiang's inner river were more convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun year 1 Junior Companion Ling Xin of the Court of Imperial Entertainments said grain ships should use Zhenjiang's inner canal.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，命糧儲河道都御史李秉通七里港口，引江水注之，且浚奔牛、新港之淤。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, ordering Grain Transport and River Course Censor-in-Chief Li Bing to open Qili Harbor mouth, draw Yangtze water to pour in, and dredge the silt at Benniu and Xingang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Bing of Grain Transport to open Qili Harbor, feed Yangtze water into it, and dredge the silt at Benniu and Xingang.

sentences.zh: 巡撫崔恭又請增置五閘。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Cui Gong also requested adding five sluices.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Cui Gong also asked that five more sluices be built.

sentences.zh: 至成化四年，閘工始成。

translations.literal: By the fourth year of Chenghua the sluice works were completed.
translations.idiomatic: The sluice works were not finished until Chenghua year 4.

sentences.zh: 於是漕舟盡由裏河，其入二河者，回空之艘及他舟而已。

translations.literal: Thus grain transports all went by the inner river; those entering the two rivers were only empty-return ships and other vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Grain traffic then used the inner canal entirely; only empty return ships and other craft took the two branch rivers.

sentences.zh: 定制，孟瀆河口與瓜、儀諸港俱三年一浚。

translations.literal: By established regulation, the Mengdu river mouth and Guazhou, Yizhen, and other harbors were all dredged every three years.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation the mouth of Mengdu and the harbors at Guazhou and Yizhen were dredged every three years.

sentences.zh: 孟瀆寬廣不甚淤，裏河不久輒涸，則又改從孟瀆。

translations.literal: Mengdu was broad and did not silt much; the inner river soon dried, and then they changed again to use Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengdu was wide and did not silt heavily, but the inner canal soon ran dry, and traffic shifted back to Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 弘治十七年，部臣復陳夏港、孟瀆遠浮大江之害，請亟浚京口淤，而引練湖灌之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Hongzhi, ministry officials again stated the harm of Xiagang and Mengdu floating far on the Great River, requesting urgent dredging of Jingkou silt and drawing Lianhu to irrigate it.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 17 ministry officials again warned of the risk of sending barges far out on the Yangtze from Xiagang and Mengdu, and urged that Jingkou be dredged at once and Lianhu Lake used to feed the channel.

sentences.zh: 詔速行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered rapid action.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the work done quickly.

sentences.zh: 正德二年復開白塔河及江口、大橋、潘家、通江四閘。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde the Baita River and the four sluices of Jiangkou, Daqiao, Panjia, and Tongjiang were reopened.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year 2 the Baita River and the Jiangkou, Daqiao, Panjia, and Tongjiang sluices were opened again.

sentences.zh: 十四年從督漕都御史臧鳳言，浚常州上下里河，漕舟無阻者五十餘載。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, following Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Zang Feng, the upper and lower inner canals at Changzhou were dredged, and grain transports were unimpeded for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, on the advice of Censor-in-Chief Zang Feng of Grain Transport, the inner canal above and below Changzhou was dredged, and grain traffic ran clear for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年又漸涸，復一浚之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli it gradually dried again, and was dredged once more.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 1 it began to dry up again and was dredged once more.

sentences.zh: 歲貢生許汝愚上言：「國初置四閘：曰京口，曰丹徒，防三江之涸；

translations.literal: Annual tribute student Xu Runyu memorialized: "At the founding of the dynasty four sluices were set: called Jingkou, called Dantu, to guard against the drying of the Three Rivers;
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute student Xu Runyu submitted: "At the founding of the dynasty four sluices were built—Jingkou and Dantu to keep the Three Rivers from running dry;

sentences.zh: 曰呂城，曰奔牛，防五湖之泄。

translations.literal: called Lücheng, called Benniu, to guard against the draining of the Five Lakes;
translations.idiomatic: Lücheng and Benniu to keep the Five Lakes from draining away;

sentences.zh: 自丹陽至鎮江蓄為湖者三：曰練湖，曰焦子，曰杜墅。

translations.literal: from Danyang to Zhenjiang stored as lakes were three: called Lianhu, called Jiaozi, called Dushu.
translations.idiomatic: and from Danyang to Zhenjiang three lakes were kept in reserve: Lianhu, Jiaozi, and Dushu.

sentences.zh: 歲久，居民侵種，焦、杜二湖俱涸，僅存練湖，猶有侵者。

translations.literal: Over the years commoners encroached to plant; Jiao and Du two lakes both dried, only Lianhu remained, and still there were encroachments.
translations.idiomatic: Over time locals encroached to farm them; Jiaozi and Dushu both dried up, and only Lianhu remained, still subject to encroachment.

sentences.zh: 而四閘俱空設矣。

translations.literal: Yet the four sluices were all set up in vain.
translations.idiomatic: The four sluices had become useless.

sentences.zh: 請浚三湖故址通漕。

translations.literal: We request dredging the former sites of the three lakes to connect grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the three lakes be restored to serve transport.

sentences.zh: 」總河傅希摯言：「練湖已浚，而焦子、杜墅源少無益。

translations.literal: Grand Canal Director Fu Xizhi said: "Lianhu has been dredged, but Jiaozi and Dushu have few sources and would be of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Canal Director Fu Xizhi replied: "Lianhu has already been dredged, but Jiaozi and Dushu have too little inflow to help."

sentences.zh: 」其議遂寢。

translations.literal: That proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，練湖復淤淺。

translations.literal: Before long Lianhu silted shallow again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lianhu silted up again.

sentences.zh: 五年，御史郭思極、陳世寶先後請復練湖，浚孟瀆。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Censors Guo Siji and Chen Shibao successively requested restoring Lianhu and dredging Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Censors Guo Siji and Chen Shibao in turn asked that Lianhu be restored and Mengdu dredged.

sentences.zh: 而給事中湯聘尹則請於京口旁別建一閘，引江流內注，潮長則開，縮則閉。

translations.literal: But Supervising Secretary Tang Pinyin requested building a separate sluice beside Jingkou, drawing river current inward—when the tide rose open it, when it ebbed close it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Tang Pinyin proposed a new sluice beside Jingkou to draw Yangtze water in, opening when the tide rose and closing when it fell.

sentences.zh: 御史尹良任又言：「孟瀆渡江入黃家港，水面雖闊，江流甚平，由此抵泰興以達灣頭、高郵僅二百餘里，可免瓜、儀不測之患。

translations.literal: Censor Yin Liangren also said: "Mengdu crosses the river into Huangjia Harbor; though the water surface is broad, the river current is very level; from here reaching Taixing to arrive at Wantou and Gaoyou is only a little more than two hundred li, and the unforeseen dangers of Guazhou and Yizhen can be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yin Liangren also said: "Crossing from Mengdu into Huangjia Harbor, though the water is wide the current is gentle; from there to Taixing and on to Wantou and Gaoyou is only a little over two hundred li, avoiding the hazards of Guazhou and Yizhen.

sentences.zh: ，至如京口北渡金山而下，中流遇風有漂溺患，宜挑甘露港夾岸洲田十餘里，以便回泊。

translations.literal: As for crossing north from Jingkou over Jinshan and going downstream, midstream if wind is met there is danger of drifting and drowning; it is fitting to dig out more than ten li of shoal fields along both banks of Ganlu Harbor for convenient turning and mooring."
translations.idiomatic: But north from Jingkou, crossing Jinshan and running downstream, midstream winds can capsize boats; he urged dredging more than ten li of shoal farmland along Ganlu Harbor for shelter and turning."

sentences.zh: 」御史林應訓又言：「自萬緣橋抵孟瀆，兩厓陡峻，雨潦易圮，且江潮湧沙，淤塞難免。

translations.literal: Censor Lin Yingxun also said: "From Wanyuan Bridge to Mengdu, both banks are steep and precipitous, rain floods easily collapse them, and Yangtze tides surge sand—silt blockage is hard to avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lin Yingxun added: "From Wanyuan Bridge to Mengdu the banks are steep, rain easily washes them away, and Yangtze sand silts the channel without fail.

sentences.zh: 宜於萬緣橋、黃連樹各建閘以資蓄泄。

translations.literal: It is fitting to build sluices at Wanyuan Bridge and Huanglianshu each to aid storage and discharge."
translations.idiomatic: Sluices should be built at Wanyuan Bridge and Huanglianshu to store and release the water."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「練湖自西晉陳敏遏馬林溪，引長山八十四溪之水以溉雲陽，堤名練塘，又曰練河，凡四十里許。

translations.literal: He also said: "Lianhu—from Western Jin Chen Min blocking Malin Stream, drawing the waters of Changshan's eighty-four streams to irrigate Yunyang—the dike was named Liantang, also called Lian River, altogether about forty li.
translations.idiomatic: He also described Lianhu: in the Western Jin, Chen Min dammed Malin Stream and drew in the eighty-four streams of Changshan to irrigate Yunyang; the embankment was called Liantang or the Lian River, about forty li long.

sentences.zh: 環湖立涵洞十三。

translations.literal: Around the lake thirteen culverts were set.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen culverts were built around the lake.

sentences.zh: 宋紹興時，中置橫埂，分上下湖，立上、中、下三閘。

translations.literal: In Song Shaoxing times a transverse embankment was placed in the middle, dividing upper and lower lakes, and upper, middle, and lower three sluices were set.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song in the Shaoxing era a cross-dike divided the upper and lower lakes, with upper, middle, and lower sluices.

sentences.zh: 八十四溪之水始經辰溪沖入上湖，復由三閘轉入下湖。

translations.literal: The waters of the eighty-four streams first passed through Chen Stream rushing into the upper lake, then by the three sluices turned into the lower lake.
translations.idiomatic: Water from the eighty-four streams first entered the upper lake through Chen Stream, then passed through the three sluices into the lower lake.

sentences.zh: 洪武間，因運道澀，依下湖東堤建三閘，借湖水以濟運，後乃漸堙。

translations.literal: During Hongwu, because the transport channel was sluggish, following the east dike of the lower lake three sluices were built, borrowing lake water to aid transport; later they gradually silted shut.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu reign, when the transport channel ran low, three sluices were built along the east dike of the lower lake to feed the canal; later they gradually silted up.

sentences.zh: 今當盡革侵佔，復浚為湖。

translations.literal: Now encroachments should all be eliminated and it dredged back into a lake.
translations.idiomatic: Encroachments should be cleared and the lake restored.

sentences.zh: 上湖四際夾阜，下湖東北臨河，原埂完固，惟應補中間缺口，且增築西南，與東北相應。

translations.literal: The upper lake on four sides is flanked by hills; the lower lake northeast faces the river; the original embankment is intact—only the middle gap should be repaired, and the southwest additionally built up to correspond with the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: The upper lake is ringed by hills; the lower lake faces the river to the northeast. The old embankment is largely intact—only the gap in the middle needs repair, with the southwest raised to match the northeast.

sentences.zh: 至三閘，惟臨湖上閘如故，宜增建中、下二閘，更設減水閘二座，界中、下二閘間。

translations.literal: As for the three sluices, only the upper sluice facing the lake remains as before; the middle and lower two sluices should be added, and two spill sluices set between the middle and lower sluices.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three sluices only the upper one by the lake still stands; the middle and lower sluices should be rebuilt, with two spill sluices between them.

sentences.zh: 共革田五千畝有奇，塞沿堤私設涵洞，止存其舊十三處，以宣洩湖水。

translations.literal: Altogether more than five thousand mu of fields would be reclaimed, private culverts along the dike blocked, only the original thirteen places kept to discharge lake water.
translations.idiomatic: This would reclaim more than five thousand mu of farmland, close private culverts along the dike, and keep only the original thirteen outlets to release lake water.

sentences.zh: 冬春即閉塞，毋得私啟。

translations.literal: In winter and spring they would be closed and blocked; none may be opened privately.
translations.idiomatic: In winter and spring they would stay closed and might not be opened without authority.

sentences.zh: 蓋練湖無源，惟藉瀦蓄，增堤啟閘，水常有餘，然後可以濟運。

translations.literal: For Lianhu has no source—it relies only on impoundment; raising dikes and opening sluices, water is always in surplus, and only then can transport be aided.
translations.idiomatic: Lianhu has no spring of its own and depends entirely on storage; with higher dikes and controlled sluices the water can be kept full enough to feed the canal.

sentences.zh: 臣親驗上湖地仰，八十四溪之水所由來，懼其易泄；

translations.literal: Your subject personally verified the upper lake's land rises; the eighty-four streams' waters come from there—I fear they drain too easily;
translations.idiomatic: I have inspected the site myself: the upper lake sits on rising ground where the eighty-four streams enter, and I fear the water drains away too easily;

sentences.zh: 下湖地平衍，僅高漕河數尺，又常懼不盈。

translations.literal: the lower lake's land is level and spreading, only a few chi higher than the grain canal, and I constantly fear it will not be full.
translations.idiomatic: the lower lake is flat and only a few feet above the grain canal, and I often fear it will not fill.

sentences.zh: 誠使水裕堤堅，則應時注之，河有全力矣。

translations.literal: If truly the water is ample and the dikes firm, then releasing it in season, the canal will have full force.
translations.idiomatic: If the water is truly ample and the dikes strong, timely release would give the canal its full force.

sentences.zh: 」皆下所司酌議。

translations.literal: All were sent down to the responsible offices for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: All these proposals were referred to the relevant offices for review.

sentences.zh: 十三年，鎮江知府吳捴謙復言：「練湖中堤宜飭有司春初即修，以防沖決，且禁勢豪侵佔。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhenjiang Prefect Wu Youqian again said: "The middle dike of Lianhu should be ordered that responsible offices repair it at the start of spring, to guard against washout, and powerful families' encroachments should be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 Zhenjiang Prefect Wu Youqian urged again: "The middle dike of Lianhu should be repaired each spring to prevent breaches, and powerful families must be barred from encroaching."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十七年浚武進橫林漕河。

translations.literal: In year 17 the Henglin grain canal at Wujin was dredged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 the Henglin grain canal at Wujin was dredged.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，浚京口漕河。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, the grain canal at Jingkou was dredged.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 1 the grain canal at Jingkou was dredged.

sentences.zh: 五年，太常少卿薑志禮建《漕河議》，言：「神廟

translations.literal: In year 5, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Jiang Zhili submitted the "Treatise on the Grain Canal," saying: "Shenmiao
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 5, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Jiang Zhili submitted the "Treatise on the Grain Canal," stating: "In the early Wanli reign—

sentences.zh: 初，先臣寶著《漕河議》，當事採行，不開河而濟運者二十餘年。

translations.literal: at the beginning, my late forebear Bao wrote the "Treatise on the Grain Canal"; those in charge adopted and implemented it, and for more than twenty years transport was aided without opening the river.
translations.idiomatic: my forebear Bao wrote the "Treatise on the Grain Canal"; the authorities adopted it, and for more than twenty years grain transport was sustained without opening new channels.

sentences.zh: 後復佃湖妨運，歲累畚鍤。

translations.literal: Later the lake was leased out again, obstructing transport, and year after year spades and mattocks piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Later the lake was leased for farming again, blocking transport, and dredging with spades and mattocks became an annual burden.

sentences.zh: 故老有言，「京口閘底與虎丘塔頂平」，是可知挑河無益，蓄湖為要也。

translations.literal: Elders have a saying, "The bottom of the Jingkou sluice is level with the top of Tiger Hill pagoda"—from this one may know dredging the river is useless and storing the lake is essential.
translations.idiomatic: Elders say, "The floor of the Jingkou sluice is level with the summit of Tiger Hill pagoda"—which shows that dredging the canal is useless and impounding the lake is what matters.

sentences.zh: 今當革佃修閘，而高築上下湖圍埂，蓄水使深。

translations.literal: Now we should abolish leasing and repair the sluices, and heighten the ring dikes of the upper and lower lakes to store water deep.
translations.idiomatic: Now leasing should be ended and the sluices repaired, and the ring dikes around the upper and lower lakes should be raised to hold a deep head of water.

sentences.zh: 且漕河閘座非僅京口、呂城、新閘、奔牛數處而已，陵口、尹公橋、黃泥壩、新豐、大犢山節節有閘，皆廢去，並宜修建。

translations.literal: Moreover, sluice sites on the grain canal are not only at Jingkou, Lücheng, Xinzha, and Benniu; at Lingkou, Yinggong Bridge, Huangniba, Xinfeng, and Dadushan there are sluices at every stage—all abandoned—and all should be rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: Sluice stations on the grain canal are not limited to Jingkou, Lücheng, Xinzha, and Benniu; Lingkou, Yinggong Bridge, Huangniba, Xinfeng, and Dadushan each had sluices in turn—all now abandoned—and every one should be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 而運道支流如武進洞子河、連江橋河、扁擔河，丹陽簡橋河、陳家橋河、七里橋河、丁議河、越瀆河，勝村溪之大壩頭，丹陽甘露港南之小閘口，皆應急修整。

translations.literal: Branch routes of the transport channel such as Wujin's Dongzi River, Lianjiang Bridge River, and Biandan River; Danyang's Jianqiao River, Chenjia Bridge River, Qili Bridge River, Dingyi River, and Yuedu River; the great dam head of Shengchun Creek; and the small sluice mouth south of Danyang's Ganlu Harbor—all need urgent repair.
translations.idiomatic: Transport branches such as Wujin's Dongzi River, Lianjiang Bridge River, and Biandan River; Danyang's Jianqiao River, Chenjia Bridge River, Qili Bridge River, Dingyi River, and Yuedu River; the great dam at Shengchun Creek; and the small sluice south of Danyang's Ganlu Harbor—all need urgent repair.

sentences.zh: 至奔牛、呂城之北，各設減水閘。

translations.literal: North of Benniu and Lücheng, a spill sluice should be set at each.
translations.idiomatic: North of Benniu and Lücheng, a spill sluice should be built at each place.

sentences.zh: 歲十月實以土，商民船盡令盤壩。

translations.literal: Every year in the tenth month earth is packed in; merchant and civilian vessels are all made to portage the dams.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the tenth month the sluices are filled with earth, and merchant and civilian boats are all made to portage the dams.

sentences.zh: 此皆舊章所當率由。

translations.literal: These are all provisions of old regulations that ought to be followed.
translations.idiomatic: These are all rules of the old regulations that should be followed without fail.

sentences.zh: 近有欲開九曲河，使運船竟從泡港閘出江，直達揚子橋，以免瓜洲啟閘稽遲者，試而後行可也。

translations.literal: Recently some wish to open the Jiuqu River so transport ships may leave directly through Paogang Sluice to the Yangtze and reach Yangzi Bridge straightaway, avoiding delay from opening the Guazhou sluices—trial before implementation would be proper.
translations.idiomatic: Some have lately proposed opening the Jiuqu River so grain barges could leave through Paogang Sluice straight into the Yangtze and reach Yangzi Bridge, avoiding the delays of opening the Guazhou sluices—a trial before full adoption would be wise.

sentences.zh: 回空糧艘及官舫，宜由江行，而於河莊設閘啟閉。

translations.literal: Empty-return grain ships and official barges should travel by the Yangtze, with sluices at Hezhuang to open and close.
translations.idiomatic: Empty return grain fleets and official barges should use the Yangtze route, with sluices at Hezhuang to control entry and exit.

sentences.zh: 數役並行，漕事乃大善矣。

translations.literal: With several projects carried out together, grain transport would be greatly improved.
translations.idiomatic: If these works were carried out together, grain transport would be greatly improved.

sentences.zh: 」議不果行。

translations.literal: The proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 江漕者，湖廣漕舟由漢、沔下潯陽，江西漕舟出章江、鄱陽而會於湖口，暨南直隸寧、太、池、安、江寧、廣德之舟，同浮大江，入儀真通江閘，以溯淮、揚入閘河。

translations.literal: River transport: Huguang grain barges go down the Han and Mian to Xunyang; Jiangxi barges leave Zhang River and Poyang and meet at Hukou; together with craft from southern Zhili's Ning, Tai, Chi, An, Jiangning, and Guangde they all float on the Great River, enter at Yizhen's Tongjiang Sluice, and go up the Huai and Yang into the sluice river.
translations.idiomatic: River transport: grain barges from Huguang descend the Han and Mian to Xunyang; Jiangxi barges leave the Zhang River and Poyang and converge at Hukou; together with vessels from Ning, Tai, Chi, An, Jiangning, and Guangde in southern Zhili they all sail the Great River, enter through Yizhen's Tongjiang Sluice, and ascend the Huai and Yang into the canal.

sentences.zh: 瓜、儀之間，運道之咽喉也。

translations.literal: Between Guazhou and Yizhen lies the throat of the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: Between Guazhou and Yizhen lies the throat of the transport route.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，餉遼卒者，從儀真上淮安，由鹽城泛海；

translations.literal: In Hongwu, for feeding Liao troops, [grain] went up from Yizhen to Huai'an and crossed the sea from Yancheng;
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, grain for Liao garrisons went up from Yizhen to Huai'an and then crossed the sea from Yancheng;

sentences.zh: 餉梁、晉者，亦從儀真赴淮安，盤壩入淮。

translations.literal: for feeding Liang and Jin, it also went from Yizhen to Huai'an and portaged the dams into the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: for Liang and Jin it likewise went from Yizhen to Huai'an and portaged the dams into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 江口則設壩置閘，凡十有三。

translations.literal: At the river mouth dams and sluices were set up—thirteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: At the river mouth dams and sluices were installed—thirteen in all.

sentences.zh: 浚揚子橋河至黃泥灣九千餘丈。

translations.literal: The Yangzi Bridge River was dredged to Huangniwan—more than nine thousand zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi Bridge River was dredged as far as Huangniwan—more than nine thousand zhang.

sentences.zh: 永樂間，浚儀真清江壩、下水港及夾港河，修沿江堤岸。

translations.literal: During Yongle, the Yizhen Qingjiang dam, Xiaoshui Harbor, and Jiagang River were dredged, and dikes along the river were repaired.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle the Yizhen Qingjiang dam, Xiaoshui Harbor, and Jiagang River were dredged, and the river dikes were repaired.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年浚儀真壩河，後定制儀真壩下黃泥灘、直河口二港及瓜洲二港、常州之孟瀆河皆三年一浚。

translations.literal: In Hongxi year 1 the Yizhen dam river was dredged; later by regulation the two harbors below the Yizhen dam—Huangnitan and Zhihekou—and the two Guazhou harbors, and Changzhou's Mengdu River, were dredged every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi year 1 the Yizhen dam river was dredged; later by regulation Huangnitan and Zhihekou below the Yizhen dam, the two Guazhou harbors, and Changzhou's Mengdu River were dredged every three years.

sentences.zh: 宣德間，從侍郎趙新、御史陳祚請，浚黃泥灘、清江閘。

translations.literal: In Xuande, at the request of Vice Minister Zhao Xin and Censor Chen Zuo, Huangnitan and Qingjiang Sluice were dredged.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande, at the request of Vice Minister Zhao Xin and Censor Chen Zuo, Huangnitan and Qingjiang Sluice were dredged.

sentences.zh: 成化中，建閘於儀真通江河港者三，江都之留潮通江者二。

translations.literal: In Chenghua three sluices were built at Yizhen's Tongjiang harbors, and two at Jiangdu's Liuchao Tongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua three sluices were built at Yizhen's Tongjiang harbors and two at Jiangdu's Liuchao Tongjiang.

sentences.zh: 已而通江港塞。

translations.literal: Later Tongjiang Harbor silted shut.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tongjiang Harbor silted shut.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，復開之，既又於總港口建閘蓄水。

translations.literal: In early Hongzhi it was opened again, and then at Zonggangkou a sluice was built to store water.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongzhi it was opened again, and then a sluice was built at Zonggangkou to impound water.

sentences.zh: 儀真、江都二縣間，有官塘五區，築閘蓄水，以溉民田，豪民佔以為業，真、揚之間運道阻梗。

translations.literal: Between Yizhen and Jiangdu were five official ponds; sluices were built to impound water to irrigate fields, but powerful families occupied them for business, and the transport channel between Yizhen and Yangzhou was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yizhen and Jiangdu lay five official ponds with sluices to store water for irrigation, but powerful families seized them for profit and the transport channel between Yizhen and Yangzhou was obstructed.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，御史秦鉞請復五塘。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year 2 Censor Qin Yue requested restoration of the five ponds.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 2 Censor Qin Yue asked that the five ponds be restored.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，御史陳世寶言：「儀真江口，去閘太遠，請於上下十數丈許增建二閘，隨湖啟閉，以截出江之船，盡令入閘，庶免遲滯。

translations.literal: In Wanli year 5 Censor Chen Shibao said: "At the Yizhen river mouth the distance from the sluice is too far; please build two additional sluices some tens of zhang above and below, opening and closing with the lake, to intercept ships heading out to the river and compel them all to enter the sluice, that delay may be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 5 Censor Chen Shibao said: "At the Yizhen river mouth the sluice is too far from the river; please add two sluices a few tens of zhang upstream and downstream, opening and closing with the lake level, to catch boats bound for the Yangtze and force them through the sluice, so delays may be avoided.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, the proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved and the plan adopted.

sentences.zh: 白塔河者，在泰州。

translations.literal: The Baita River lies in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Baita River lies in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 上通邵伯，下接大江，斜對常州孟瀆河與泰興北新河，皆浙漕間道也。

translations.literal: Upstream it connects to Shaobo; downstream it joins the Great River; it faces Changzhou's Mengdu River and Taixing's Beixin River obliquely—all bypaths of Zhejiang grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: It connects upstream to Shaobo and downstream to the Great River; obliquely across lie Changzhou's Mengdu River and Taixing's Beixin River—all alternate routes for Zhejiang grain transport.

sentences.zh: 自陳瑄始開。

translations.literal: It was first opened by Chen Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: It was first opened by Chen Xuan.

sentences.zh: 宣德間，從趙新、陳祚請，命瑄役夫四萬五千餘人浚之，建新閘、潘家莊、大橋、江口四閘。

translations.literal: In Xuande, at Zhao Xin and Chen Zuo's request, he was ordered with forty-five thousand laborers to dredge it, building four sluices: Xinzha, Panjiazhuang, Daqiao, and Jiangkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande, at the request of Zhao Xin and Chen Zuo, Chen Xuan was ordered to dredge it with more than forty-five thousand laborers, building four sluices at Xinzha, Panjiazhuang, Daqiao, and Jiangkou.

sentences.zh: 正統四年，水潰閘塞，都督武興因閉不用，仍自瓜洲盤壩。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong year 4 flood burst the sluices; Commissioner-in-chief Wu Xing closed them and stopped using them, and [traffic] still portaged the dams at Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 4 floods burst the sluices; Commissioner-in-chief Wu Xing closed them and abandoned the route, and traffic still portaged the dams at Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 瓜洲之壩，洪武中置，凡十五，列東西二港間。

translations.literal: The dams at Guazhou were placed in Hongwu—fifteen in all, ranged between the eastern and western harbors.
translations.idiomatic: The dams at Guazhou were established in Hongwu—fifteen in all, set between the eastern and western harbors.

sentences.zh: 永樂間，廢東壩為廠，以貯材木，止存西港七壩。

translations.literal: During Yongle the eastern dams were abolished for a depot to store timber; only seven western-harbor dams remained.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle the eastern dams were turned into a timber depot; only seven dams at the western harbor remained.

sentences.zh: 漕舟失泊，屢遭風險。

translations.literal: Grain barges lost anchorage and repeatedly met wind peril.
translations.idiomatic: Grain barges lost safe anchorage and repeatedly met danger in high winds.

sentences.zh: 英宗初年，乃復浚東港。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Yingzong the eastern harbor was dredged again.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Emperor Yingzong the eastern harbor was dredged again.

sentences.zh: 既而巡撫周忱築壩白塔河之大橋閘，以時啟閉，漕舟稍分行。

translations.literal: Later Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen built a dam at the Daqiao sluice on the Baita River, opening and closing on schedule, and grain barges gradually divided between routes.
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen built a dam at the Daqiao sluice on the Baita River, opening and closing it on schedule, and grain barges gradually split between routes.

sentences.zh: 自鎮江裏河開浚，漕舟出甘露、新港，徑渡瓜洲；

translations.literal: Once the inner canal at Zhenjiang was dredged open, grain barges left by Ganlu and Xingang and crossed straight to Guazhou;
translations.idiomatic: Once the inner canal at Zhenjiang was dredged open, grain barges left through Ganlu and Xingang and crossed straight to Guazhou;

sentences.zh: 而白塔、北新，皆以江路險遠，舍而不由矣。

translations.literal: while Baita and Beixin, because the Yangtze route was perilous and far, were abandoned and no longer used.
translations.idiomatic: while Baita and Beixin, because the Yangtze route was dangerous and distant, were set aside and no longer used.

sentences.zh: 衛漕者，即衛河。

translations.literal: Wei transport—that is, the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Wei transport is the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 源出河南輝縣，至臨清與會通河合，北達天津。

translations.literal: Its source is in Huixian, Henan; at Linqing it joins the Huitong River and reaches north to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: It rises in Huixian, Henan; at Linqing it joins the Huitong River and runs north to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 自臨清以北皆稱衛河。

translations.literal: From Linqing northward all is called the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: From Linqing northward the whole course is called the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 詳具本《志》。

translations.literal: Details are given in full in this Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in this Treatise.

sentences.zh: 白漕者，即通濟河。

translations.literal: Bai transport—that is, the Tongji River.
translations.idiomatic: Bai transport is the Tongji River.

sentences.zh: 源出塞地，經密雲縣霧靈山，為潮河川。

translations.literal: Its source is in the frontier; through Miyun's Wuling Mountain it becomes the Chao River.
translations.idiomatic: It rises in the frontier; passing Miyun's Wuling Mountain it becomes the Chao River.

sentences.zh: 而富河、罾口河、七渡河、桑乾河、三里河俱會於此，名曰白河。

translations.literal: The Fu, Zengkou, Qidu, Sanggan, and Sanli rivers all meet here and are named the Bai River.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu, Zengkou, Qidu, Sanggan, and Sanli rivers all converge here and are called the Bai River.

sentences.zh: 南流經通州，合通惠及榆、渾諸河，亦名潞河。

translations.literal: Flowing south through Tongzhou, it joins the Tonghui and Yu and Hun rivers, and is also called the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: It flows south through Tongzhou, joins the Tonghui and Yu and Hun rivers, and is also called the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 三百六十里，至直沽會衛河入海，賴以通漕。

translations.literal: Three hundred and sixty li to Zhigu it meets the Wei River and enters the sea—on this grain transport depends.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred and sixty li to Zhigu it meets the Wei River and enters the sea—grain transport depends on this course.

sentences.zh: 楊村以北，勢若建瓴，底多淤沙。

translations.literal: North of Yangcun the gradient is like water poured from a high jar; the bottom holds much silt sand.
translations.idiomatic: North of Yangcun the slope is steep as a tilted jar, and the bed holds much silt.

sentences.zh: 夏秋水漲苦潦，冬春水微苦澀。

translations.literal: In summer and autumn floods bring distress; in winter and spring low water brings bitter brackishness.
translations.idiomatic: In summer and autumn floods are a plague; in winter and spring low water turns brackish.

sentences.zh: 沖潰徙改頗與黃河同。

translations.literal: Scouring breaks and course shifts resemble the Yellow River in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: Breaches and channel shifts resemble those of the Yellow River in many ways.

sentences.zh: 耎兒渡者，在武清、通州間，尤其要害處也。

translations.literal: Ruan'er Ford lies between Wuqing and Tongzhou—the most critical point.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan'er Ford, between Wuqing and Tongzhou, is the most critical point of all.

sentences.zh: 自永樂至成化初年，凡八決，輒發民夫築堤。

translations.literal: From Yongle to early Chenghua it burst eight times, and each time corvée labor was sent to build dikes.
translations.idiomatic: From Yongle to early Chenghua it broke eight times, and each time corvée labor was sent to build dikes.

sentences.zh: 而正統元年之決，為害尤甚，特敕太監沐敬、安遠侯柳溥、尚書李友直隨宜區畫，發五軍營卒五萬及民夫一萬築決堤。

translations.literal: The breach of Zhengtong year 1 did the most harm; an especial decree ordered Eunuch Mu Jing, Marquis of Anyuan Liu Bo, and Minister Li Youzhi to plan as appropriate, sending fifty thousand troops from the Five Military Camps and ten thousand laborers to repair the breach dike.
translations.idiomatic: The breach of Zhengtong year 1 did the worst damage; a special decree ordered Eunuch Mu Jing, Marquis of Anyuan Liu Bo, and Minister Li Youzhi to plan as needed, with fifty thousand troops from the Five Military Camps and ten thousand laborers to repair the broken dike.

sentences.zh: 又命武進伯硃冕、尚書吳中役五萬人，去河西務二十里鑿河一道，導白水入其中。

translations.literal: Zhu Mian, Military Count of Wujin, and Minister Wu Zhong were also ordered to mobilize fifty thousand men and dig a channel twenty li west of Hexiwu to conduct white water into it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mian, Military Count of Wujin, and Minister Wu Zhong were also ordered to mobilize fifty thousand men and cut a channel twenty li west of Hexiwu to lead the Bai River into it.

sentences.zh: 二工並竣，人甚便之，賜河名曰通濟，封河神曰通濟河神。

translations.literal: When both projects were finished people found them very convenient; the river was granted the name Tongji and the river god enfeoffed as God of the Tongji River.
translations.idiomatic: When both works were finished the people found them very convenient; the river was named Tongji, and the river god was enfeoffed as God of the Tongji River.

sentences.zh: 先是，永樂二十一年築通州抵直沽河岸，有沖決者，隨時修築以為常。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Yongle year 21 the bank from Tongzhou to Zhigu was built; where it breached, repair followed at once as routine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Yongle year 21 the bank from Tongzhou to Zhigu was built; wherever it broke, repair at once became routine.

sentences.zh: 迨通濟河成，決岸修築者亦且數四。

translations.literal: Once the Tongji River was complete, breaches in the bank were repaired some four times as well.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tongji River was finished, the bank was repaired for breaches some four times as well.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十一年從工部議，挑通州至天津白河，深四尺五寸，所挑沙土即築堤兩岸，著為令。

translations.literal: In Wanli year 31, following the Ministry of Works' proposal, the Bai River from Tongzhou to Tianjin was dredged to a depth of four chi five cun; the excavated sand and earth were used to build dikes on both banks—this was made regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 31, following the Ministry of Works, the Bai River from Tongzhou to Tianjin was dredged to four chi five cun; the spoil was piled into dikes on both banks—this was made permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 大通河者，元郭守敬所鑿。

translations.literal: The Datong River was cut by Guo Shoujing of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Datong River was excavated by the Yuan's Guo Shoujing.

sentences.zh: 由大通橋東下，抵通州高麗莊，與白河合，至直沽，會衛河入海，長百六十里有奇。

translations.literal: From east of Datong Bridge down to Tongzhou's Gaoli Zhuang it joins the Bai River to Zhigu, meets the Wei River and enters the sea—more than one hundred and sixty li long.
translations.idiomatic: From east of Datong Bridge down to Tongzhou's Gaoli Zhuang it joins the Bai River to Zhigu, meets the Wei River and enters the sea—a course of more than one hundred and sixty li.

sentences.zh: 十里一閘，蓄水濟運，名曰通惠。

translations.literal: Every ten li a sluice, storing water to aid transport—named Tonghui.
translations.idiomatic: A sluice every ten li impounded water for transport—it was named Tonghui.

sentences.zh: 又以白河、榆河、渾河合流，亦名潞河。

translations.literal: Because the Bai, Yu, and Hun rivers join in confluence, it is also called the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Bai, Yu, and Hun rivers join in confluence, it is also called the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 洪武中漸廢。

translations.literal: In Hongwu it was gradually abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu it was gradually abandoned.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年八月，北京行部言：「宛平昌平西湖、景東牛欄莊及青龍華家ＢＧ1111山三閘，水沖決岸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Yongle year 4 the Beijing Branch Ministry reported: "The three sluices at Changping's West Lake, Jingdong Niulanzhuang, and Qinglong Huajia [corrupted text: BG1111] Mountain—waters have scoured and breached the banks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongle year 4 the Beijing regional office reported: "At West Lake and Jingdong Niulanzhuang in Changping, and at Qinglong Huajia Mountain—three sluices where floodwaters have breached the banks.

sentences.zh: 」命發軍民修治。

translations.literal: An order was issued to mobilize soldiers and civilians for repairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered soldiers and civilians mobilized for repairs.

sentences.zh: 明年復言：「自西湖、景東至通流，凡七閘，河道淤塞。

translations.literal: The next year they reported again: "From West Lake and Jingdong to Tongliu, seven sluices in all—the channel is silted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they reported again: "From West Lake and Jingdong to Tongliu, seven sluices in all—the channel is silted shut.

sentences.zh: 自昌平東南白浮村至西湖、景東流水河口一百里，宜增置十二閘。

translations.literal: From Baifu Village southeast of Changping to the West Lake and Jingdong drainage mouths—one hundred li—twelve additional sluices should be built.
translations.idiomatic: From Baifu Village southeast of Changping to the drainage mouths at West Lake and Jingdong—a stretch of one hundred li—twelve more sluices should be added.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，閘俱堙，不復通舟。

translations.literal: Before long all sluices were buried and boats could no longer pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before long all the sluices silted over and boats could no longer pass.

sentences.zh: 成化中，漕運總兵官楊茂言：「每歲自張家灣舍舟，車轉至都下，僱值不貲。

translations.literal: In Chenghua the Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Yang Mao said: "Each year at Zhangjiawan one abandons the boats and carts goods to the capital—the hire costs are immense.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua the Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Yang Mao said: "Each year at Zhangjiawan we leave the boats and cart grain to the capital—the hire costs are enormous.

sentences.zh: 舊通惠河石閘尚存，深二尺許，修閘瀦水，用小舟剝運便。

translations.literal: The stone sluices of the old Tonghui River still survive, two chi or so deep; repair the sluices to pond water and lighter transport by small boats would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The stone sluices of the old Tonghui River still stand, two chi or so deep; if the sluices were repaired to hold water, lighterage by small boats would be far easier.

sentences.zh: 」又有議於三里河從張家灣煙墩橋以西疏河泊舟者。

translations.literal: There was also a proposal to dredge the Sanli River west of Zhangjiawan's Yandun Bridge to berth boats.
translations.idiomatic: Others proposed dredging the Sanli River west of Zhangjiawan's Yandun Bridge to berth boats.

sentences.zh: 下廷臣集議，遣尚書楊鼎、侍郎喬毅相度。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministry for joint deliberation, and Ministers Yang Ding and Qiao Yi were sent to survey.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the ministries for joint deliberation, and Ministers Yang Ding and Qiao Yi were sent to survey the ground.

sentences.zh: 上言：「舊閘二十四座，通水行舟。

translations.literal: They memorialized: "Of the old twenty-four sluices, water passed and boats traveled.
translations.idiomatic: They reported: "Of the old twenty-four sluices, water flowed and boats passed.

sentences.zh: 但元時水在宮牆外，舟得入城內海子灣。

translations.literal: But in Yuan times the water lay outside the palace walls and boats could enter the inner-city Haiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuan times the water lay outside the palace walls and boats could enter the inner-city reservoir.

sentences.zh: 今水從皇城金水河出，故道不可復行。

translations.literal: Now water issues from the imperial-city Jinshui River, so the old course cannot be used again.
translations.idiomatic: Now the water leaves through the imperial-city Jinshui River, so the old course cannot be restored.

sentences.zh: 且元引白浮泉往西逆流，今經山陵，恐妨地脈。

translations.literal: Moreover the Yuan drew the Baifu spring westward against the current; today it would pass imperial tombs and might harm the geomantic pulse.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Yuan diverted the Baifu spring westward against the current; today that would pass the imperial tombs and might disturb the geomantic pulse.

sentences.zh: 又一畝泉過白羊口山溝，兩水沖截難引。

translations.literal: Also the Yimu spring passes the gully of Baiyangkou Mountain—two waters clash and are hard to divert.
translations.idiomatic: The Yimu spring also runs through the gully at Baiyangkou Mountain—two currents collide and are hard to lead away.

sentences.zh: 若城南三里河舊無河源，正統間修城壕，恐雨多水溢，乃穿正陽橋東南□□下地，開壕口以泄之，始有三里河名。

translations.literal: If the Sanli River south of the city formerly had no river source—in Zhengtong when the city moat was repaired, fearing overflow in heavy rain, they bored southeast from Zhengyang Bridge through [lacuna] low ground and opened a moat outlet to drain it—the name Sanli River then arose.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city the old Sanli River had no natural source; during the Zhengtong repair of the city moat, fearing rain would raise the water too high, they cut through low-lying ground southeast of Zhengyang Bridge and opened a moat outlet to drain it, and only then was it called the Sanli River.

sentences.zh: 自壕口八里，始接渾河。

translations.literal: From the moat outlet eight li farther on it joins the Hun River.
translations.idiomatic: Eight li from the moat outlet it joins the Hun River.

sentences.zh: 舊渠兩岸多廬墓，水淺河窄，又須增引別流相濟。

translations.literal: Along the old channel both banks have many reed huts and tombs; the water is shallow and the river narrow, and additional diversion from other streams is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Along the old channel both banks are crowded with reed huts and tombs; the water is shallow and the river narrow, and extra diversion from other streams would be needed.

sentences.zh: 如西湖草橋源出玉匠局、馬跑等地，泉不深遠。

translations.literal: Such sources as West Lake's Caoqiao, issuing from the Jade Crafts Bureau and Mapao and other places—the springs are not deep or far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Sources such as West Lake's Caoqiao, fed from the Jade Crafts Bureau, Mapao, and other places, are neither deep nor far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 元人曾用金口水，洶湧沒民舍，以故隨廢。

translations.literal: The Yuan once used Jinshui, which surged and drowned commoners' houses, and for that reason was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan once used Jinshui, which surged and drowned commoners' houses, and for that reason abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 惟玉泉、龍泉及月兒、柳沙等泉，皆出西北，循山麓而行，可導入西湖。

translations.literal: Only the Yuquan, Longquan, and Yue'er, Liusha, and other springs—all issue northwest, running along the mountain foot, and can be led into West Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Yuquan, Longquan, Yue'er, Liusha, and other springs—all rise in the northwest and run along the foothills—can be led into West Lake.

sentences.zh: 請浚西湖之源，閉分水清龍閘，引諸泉水從高梁河，分其半由金水河出，餘則從都城外壕流轉，會於正陽門東。

translations.literal: Please dredge the source of West Lake, close the Fenzhang Qinglong sluice, and lead all springs from Gaoliang River—half by the Jinshui River out [of the palace], the rest turning outside the capital moat to meet east of Zhengyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dredge the source of West Lake, close the Fenzhang Qinglong sluice, and lead all these springs from Gaoliang River—half out through the Jinshui River, the rest circling outside the capital moat to meet east of Zhengyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 城壕且閉，令勿入三里河並流。

translations.literal: Close the city moat as well so it does not merge into the Sanli River current.
translations.idiomatic: Close the city moat as well so it does not join the Sanli River flow.

sentences.zh: 大通橋閘河隨旱澇啟閉，則舟獲近倉，甚便。

translations.literal: The Datong Bridge sluice-river should open and close with drought and flood, and then boats can reach the granaries nearby—very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The Datong Bridge sluice-river should open and close with drought and flood, and then boats can reach the granaries nearby—very convenient.

sentences.zh: 」帝從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 方發軍夫九萬修浚，會以災異，詔罷諸役。

translations.literal: Just as ninety thousand laborers were sent to dredge, omens and disasters occurred and an edict halted all projects.
translations.idiomatic: Just as ninety thousand laborers were sent to dredge, omens and disasters appeared and an edict halted all the works.

sentences.zh: 所司以漕事大，乃命四萬人浚城壕，而西山、玉泉及抵張家灣河道，則以漸及焉。

translations.literal: The responsible office, because grain transport was urgent, then ordered forty thousand men to dredge the city moat, while the channels from the western hills and Yuquan to Zhangjiawan would be done gradually.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office, because grain transport was pressing, then ordered forty thousand men to dredge the city moat, while the channels from the western hills and Yuquan to Zhangjiawan would be tackled step by step.

sentences.zh: 越五年，乃敕平江伯陳銳，副都御史李裕，侍郎翁世資、王詔督漕卒浚通惠河，如鼎、毅前議。

translations.literal: Five years later an edict ordered Military Count Chen Rui, Vice Censor-in-chief Li Yu, and Vice Ministers Weng Shizi and Wang Zhao to supervise grain-transport troops dredging the Tonghui River as in Ding and Yi's earlier proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later an edict ordered Military Count Chen Rui, Vice Censor-in-chief Li Yu, and Vice Ministers Weng Shizi and Wang Zhao to supervise grain-transport troops dredging the Tonghui River as Ding and Yi had proposed.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，工成，自大通橋至張家灣渾河口六十餘里，浚泉三，增閘四，漕舟稍通。

translations.literal: The next year, sixth month, the work was finished—from Datong Bridge to Zhangjiawan's Hun River mouth, more than sixty li; three springs dredged, four sluices added; grain barges could pass somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the sixth month, the work was finished—from Datong Bridge to Zhangjiawan's Hun River mouth, more than sixty li; three springs were dredged and four sluices added; grain barges could pass in part.

sentences.zh: 然元時所引昌平三泉俱遏不行，獨引一西湖，又僅分其半，河窄易盈涸。

translations.literal: Yet the three Changping springs the Yuan had drawn were all blocked and unused; only one West Lake was led, and even that only half its flow—the river was narrow and easily flooded or dried.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the three Changping springs the Yuan had diverted were all blocked off; only West Lake was led in, and even that at half strength—the channel was narrow and prone to flood or run dry.

sentences.zh: 不二載，澀滯如舊。

translations.literal: Within two years, silting and blockage were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years, silting and sluggish flow had returned as before.

sentences.zh: 正德二年嘗一浚之，且修大通橋至通州閘十有二，壩四十有一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde it was dredged once, and twelve sluices from Datong Bridge to Tongzhou were repaired, with forty-one dams.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde (1507) the channel was dredged once; twelve sluices from Datong Bridge to Tongzhou were repaired, and forty-one dams restored.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，御史吳仲言：「通惠河屢經修復，皆為權勢所撓。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing, Censor Wu Zhong said: "The Tonghui River has been repaired many times, yet each time thwarted by powerful interests.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing (1527), Censor Wu Zhong memorialized: "The Tonghui River has been restored again and again, yet each time powerful interests have obstructed the work.

sentences.zh: 顧通流等八閘遺跡俱存，因而成之，為力甚易，歲可省車費貲二十餘萬。

translations.literal: But the traces of the eight sluices including Tongliu all remain; completing it thereby is very easy, and yearly carriage costs of more than two hundred thousand could be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sites of the eight sluices, including Tongliu, are still there; finishing the work would be easy, and more than two hundred thousand taels in carting costs could be saved each year.

sentences.zh: 且歷代漕運皆達京師，未有貯國儲於五十里外者。

translations.literal: Moreover, through the ages grain transport all reached the capital; never was national reserve stored more than fifty li outside.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, through every dynasty grain transport had reached the capital; never had the state storehouses been kept more than fifty li away.

sentences.zh: 」帝心以為然，命侍郎王軏、何詔及仲偕相度。

translations.literal: " The emperor inwardly agreed, ordering Vice Ministers Wang Yun, He Zhao, and Zhong together to survey.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was persuaded, and ordered Vice Ministers Wang Yun and He Zhao, together with Zhong, to conduct a joint survey.

sentences.zh: 軏等言：「大通橋地形高白河六丈餘，若浚至七丈，引白河達京城，諸閘可盡罷，然未易議也。

translations.literal: Yun and others said: "Datong Bridge's terrain is more than six zhang above the Bai River; if dredged to seven zhang, drawing the Bai River to the capital, all sluices could be abolished—yet this is not easy to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and his colleagues reported: "The ground at Datong Bridge stands more than six zhang above the Bai River; dredged to seven zhang, the Bai could be led straight into the capital and every sluice dispensed with—but that proposal is not yet ripe for decision.

sentences.zh: 計獨浚治河閘，但通流閘在通州舊城中，經二水門，南浦、土橋、廣利三閘皆闤闠衢市，不便轉挽。

translations.literal: The plan is solely to dredge and treat the river sluices; but Tongliu Sluice lies in old Tongzhou city, passing two water gates; Nanpu, Tuqiao, and Guangli—three sluices—all lie amid market streets and shops, inconvenient for transshipment.
translations.idiomatic: They reckoned on dredging the river sluices alone; but Tongliu Sluice stood inside old Tongzhou, passing two water gates, and Nanpu, Tuqiao, and Guangli—the three sluices—lay in crowded market quarters where transshipment was awkward.

sentences.zh: 惟白河濱舊小河廢壩西，不一里至堰水小壩，宜修築之，使通普濟閘，可省四閘兩關轉搬力。

translations.literal: Only west of the abandoned dam on the old small river along the Bai River bank, less than one li to Yanshui minor dam, should be built up, connecting to Puji Sluice, saving the labor of transshipment at four sluices and two passes.
translations.idiomatic: West of the abandoned dam on the old creek beside the Bai River, less than a li from the Yanshui minor dam, they proposed repair so the channel would reach Puji Sluice—eliminating transshipment at four sluices and two customs passes.

sentences.zh: 」而尚書桂萼言不便，請改修三里河。

translations.literal: " But Minister Gui E said it was inconvenient and asked to shift repairs to the Sanli River.
translations.idiomatic: " But Minister Gui E objected and urged that repairs be redirected to the Sanli River instead.

sentences.zh: 帝下其疏於大學士楊一清、張璁。

translations.literal: The emperor sent his memorial down to Grand Secretaries Yang Yiqing and Zhang Cong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the memorial to Grand Secretaries Yang Yiqing and Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 一清言：「因舊閘行轉搬法，省運軍勞費，宜斷行之。

translations.literal: Yiqing said: "Following the old sluices with the transshipment method saves transport troops' labor and expense; it should be decided and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing argued: "Using the existing sluices with transshipment will spare the transport corps labor and expense—the plan should be approved outright.

sentences.zh: 」璁亦言：「此一勞永逸之計，萼所論費廣功難。

translations.literal: " Cong also said: "This is a plan of one effort, lasting benefit; what E discusses is costly and hard to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Cong added: "This is a single undertaking meant to last for generations; Gui E's scheme would be costly and hard to finish.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃卻萼議。

translations.literal: " The emperor then rejected E's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then set aside Gui E's proposal.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，仲報河成，因疏五事，言：「大通橋至通州石壩，地勢高四丈，流沙易淤，宜時加浚治。

translations.literal: The next year, sixth month, Zhong reported the river complete, and by memorial five matters, saying: "From Datong Bridge to Tongzhou stone dam, the terrain is four zhang high; drifting sand silts easily; dredging should be added from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the sixth month, Zhong reported the river finished and submitted five recommendations: "From Datong Bridge to Tongzhou's stone dam the bed rises four zhang; drifting sand silts easily, and dredging should be kept up regularly.

sentences.zh: 管河主事宜專委任，毋令兼他務。

translations.literal: The chief in charge of the river should be solely appointed, not ordered to combine other duties.
translations.idiomatic: The official in charge of the river should have sole responsibility and no collateral duties.

sentences.zh: 官吏、閘夫以罷運裁減，宜復舊額。

translations.literal: Officials, clerks, and sluice laborers were cut because transport was halted; the old quotas should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and sluice workers had been cut when transport was suspended; their former quotas should be restored.

sentences.zh: 慶豐上閘、平津中閘今已不用，宜改建通州西水關外。

translations.literal: Qingfeng upper sluice and Pingjin middle sluice are now unused; they should be rebuilt outside Tongzhou's west water gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qingfeng Upper Sluice and Pingjin Middle Sluice, now disused, should be rebuilt outside Tongzhou's west water gate.

sentences.zh: 剝船造費及遞歲修艌，俱宜酌處。

translations.literal: Costs for building lighter boats and annual repair of barges should all be weighed and arranged.
translations.idiomatic: The cost of building lighters and the annual upkeep of barges should all be reconsidered and provided for.

sentences.zh: 」帝以先朝屢勘行未即功，仲等四閱月工成，詔予賞，悉從其所請。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because the previous reign had repeatedly surveyed and carried out yet achieved nothing promptly, Zhong and others finished work in four months—the edict granted rewards and fully granted his requests.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor noted that under the previous reign surveys had been made and work begun again and again without timely success; Zhong and his team finished in four months. He issued rewards and granted every request.

sentences.zh: 仲又請留督工郎中何棟專理其事，為經久計。

translations.literal: Zhong further asked to retain Supervising Director He Dong to specialize in managing the matter, as a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong also asked that Supervising Director He Dong be kept on to manage the project permanently.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The request] was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 九年擢棟右通政，仍管通惠河道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Dong was promoted Right Commissioner of Transmission, still managing the Tonghui River course.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1530) He Dong was promoted to Right Commissioner of Transmission while continuing to oversee the Tonghui River.

sentences.zh: 是時，仲出為處州知府，進所編《通惠河志》。

translations.literal: At this time Zhong went out as prefect of Chuzhou, presenting his compiled "Gazetteer of the Tonghui River."
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhong had been appointed prefect of Chuzhou and presented his compiled Gazetteer of the Tonghui River.

sentences.zh: 帝命送史館，採入《會典》，且頒工部刊行。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered it sent to the Historiography Institute, excerpted into the "Collected Statutes," and also issued by the Ministry of Works for publication.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered it sent to the Historiography Institute, excerpted into the Collected Statutes, and published by the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 自此漕艘直達京師，迄於明末。

translations.literal: From this grain barges reached the capital directly, until the end of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: From that point grain barges sailed straight to the capital, and did so until the dynasty's fall.

sentences.zh: 人思仲德，建祠通州祀之。

translations.literal: People remembered Zhong's virtue and built a shrine at Tongzhou to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: People cherished Wu Zhong's service; a shrine was built at Tongzhou in his honor.

sentences.zh: 豐潤環香河者，浚自成化間，運粟十餘萬石以餉薊州東路者也。

translations.literal: The Fengrun ring around the Xianghe River—dredged from the Chenghua era onward—transported more than a hundred thousand shi of grain to supply the eastern route of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengrun-Xianghe canal, dredged starting in the Chenghua reign, moved more than a hundred thousand shi of grain to supply Jizhou's eastern garrison route.

sentences.zh: 後堙廢，餉改薊州給，大不便。

translations.literal: Later it silted and was abandoned; rations were shifted to Jizhou supply—greatly inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Later it silted up and was abandoned; supplies were issued from Jizhou instead, which was highly inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十五年從御史鮑承廕請，復之，且建三閘於北濟、張官屯、鴉鴻橋以瀦水。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Jiajing, following Censor Bao Chengyin's request, it was restored, and three sluices built at Beiji, Zhangguantun, and Yahong Bridge to impound water.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Jiajing (1566), on Censor Bao Chengyin's memorial, the canal was restored and three sluices built at Beiji, Zhangguantun, and Yahong Bridge to store water.

sentences.zh: 海運，始於元至元中。

translations.literal: Sea transport began in the Zhiyuan era of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sea transport began in the Yuan dynasty's Zhiyuan period.

sentences.zh: 伯顏用硃清、張瑄運糧輸京師，僅四萬餘石。

translations.literal: Bayan used Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan to transport grain to the capital—only a little more than forty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan employed Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan to ship grain to the capital—only some forty thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 其後日增，至三百萬餘石。

translations.literal: Afterward it increased daily, reaching more than three million shi.
translations.idiomatic: Volumes rose year by year until they exceeded three million shi.

sentences.zh: 初，海道萬三千餘里，最險惡，既而開生道，稍徑直。

translations.literal: At first the sea route was more than thirteen thousand li, most perilous; later the "live route" was opened, somewhat more direct.
translations.idiomatic: At first the route ran more than thirteen thousand li through the open sea and was extremely dangerous; later a coastal "live route" was opened that was somewhat straighter.

sentences.zh: 後殷明略又開新道，尤便。

translations.literal: Later Yin Minglue opened a new route, especially convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yin Minglue opened yet another route that was still more convenient.

sentences.zh: 然皆出大洋，風利，自浙西抵京不過旬日，而漂失甚多。

translations.literal: Yet all went out into the great ocean; winds favorable, from western Zhejiang to the capital in not more than ten days—but drift-loss was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all these courses lay on the open ocean; with fair winds one could reach the capital from western Zhejiang in under ten days, but losses from wreck and drift were enormous.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月復罷海運，惟存遮洋一總，運遼、薊糧。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, fifth month, sea transport was again abolished; only the single Zheyang command remained, to transport grain for Liaodong and Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, in the fifth month, sea transport was abolished again; only the Zheyang command was kept on to ship grain for Liaodong and Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年減登州衛海船百艘為十八艘，以五艘運青、萊、登布花鈔錠十二萬餘斤，歲賞遼軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong, Dengzhou guard sea ships were reduced from one hundred to eighteen; five ships transported cloth, cotton, and ingots from Qing, Lai, Deng—more than a hundred twenty thousand jin—yearly to reward Liaodong troops.
