translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong (1448) Dengzhou Guard's fleet was cut from a hundred vessels to eighteen; five ships carried more than 120,000 jin of cloth and ingots from Qingzhou, Laizhou, and Dengzhou each year as rewards for the Liaodong garrison.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年，侍郎丘浚進大學衍義補，請尋海運故道與河漕並行，大略言：「海舟一載千石，可當河舟三，用卒大減。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua, Vice Minister Qiu Jun presented his Supplement to the Great Learning, asking to seek the old sea-transport route to run parallel with canal transport, broadly saying: "A sea ship carries a thousand shi, equal to three river ships; troops used are greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua (1487), Vice Minister Qiu Jun presented his Supplement to the Great Learning and urged that the old sea route be reopened to run alongside the canal, arguing in substance: "A sea-going vessel carries a thousand shi—the load of three river barges—and needs far fewer men.

sentences.zh: 河漕視陸運費省什三，海運視陸省什七，雖有漂溺患，然省牽卒之勞、駁淺之費、挨次之守，利害亦相當。

translations.literal: Canal transport compared with land transport saves seven-tenths in cost; sea transport compared with land saves seven-tenths; though there is the calamity of drift and drowning, yet saving the labor of hauling troops, the expense of lightering shallows, and the waiting at relay stations—the benefit and harm are also comparable.
translations.idiomatic: Canal transport cost one-third less than overland haulage; sea transport seven-tenths less. Wreck and drowning remained a risk, but one spared the toil of draft teams, the cost of lightering shallows, and the delays at relay stations—the trade-offs roughly balanced.

sentences.zh: 宜訪素知海道者，講求勘視。

translations.literal: Those who know the sea route from of old should be sought to discuss and survey.
translations.idiomatic: Experts who knew the sea lanes should be consulted and the route surveyed.

sentences.zh: 」其說未行。

translations.literal: " This plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，河決金龍口，有請復海運者，朝議弗是。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi, the river broke at Jinlong Mouth; some asked to restore sea transport—the court discussion was not in favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi (1492), when the Yellow River burst at Jinlong Mouth, some urged a return to sea transport, but the court rejected the idea.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，遮洋總漂糧二萬石，溺死官軍五十餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, the Zheyang command drift-lost twenty thousand shi of grain; more than fifty officers and troops drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing (1523), the Zheyang command lost twenty thousand shi of grain to wreck and drift, and more than fifty officers and soldiers drowned.

sentences.zh: 五年停登州造船。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Dengzhou shipbuilding was halted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1526) shipbuilding at Dengzhou was suspended.

sentences.zh: 二十年，總河王以旂以河道梗澀，言：「海運雖難行，然中間平度州東南有南北新河一道，元時建閘直達安東，南北悉由內洋而行，路捷無險，所當講求。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Grand Canal Director Wang Yiqin, because the canal was choked and sluggish, said: "Though sea transport is hard to run, yet midway, southeast of Pingduzhou, there is a north-south New River channel; in Yuan times sluices were built reaching straight to Andong; north and south all went by inner sea—route swift, without peril—what ought to be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1541), Grand Canal Director Wang Yiqin, finding the canal silted and sluggish, argued: "Sea transport may be hard to revive, but midway, southeast of Pingdu, there is a north-south New River that the Yuan had sluiced straight through to Andong; traffic north and south ran inside the coastal waters—swift and safe—and ought to be investigated.

sentences.zh: 」帝以海道迂遠，卻其議。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because the sea route was circuitous and far, rejected the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor dismissed the plan as too long and indirect a sea route.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，遼東巡撫侯汝諒言：「天津入遼之路，自海口至右屯河通堡不及二百里，其中曹泊店、月坨桑、薑女墳、桃花島皆可灣泊。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, Liaodong Grand Coordinator Hou Ruliang said: "The route from Tianjin into Liaodong—from the sea mouth to the Right Tun River pass-fort, less than two hundred li; among them Caobodian, Yuetuo Hill, Jiangnü Grave, and Peach Blossom Island can all be moored in the lee.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year (1559), Liaodong Grand Coordinator Hou Ruliang reported: "The passage from Tianjin into Liaodong—from the estuary to the Right Tun River pass-fort is under two hundred li; Caobodian, Yuetuo Hill, Jiangnü Grave, and Peach Blossom Island all offer sheltered anchorages.

sentences.zh: 」部覆行之。

translations.literal: " The ministry reviewed and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry approved and implemented the plan.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，順天巡撫耿隨朝勘海道，自永平西下海，百四十五里至紀各莊，又四百二十六里至天津，皆傍岸行舟。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, Shuntian Grand Coordinator Geng Suichao surveyed the sea route—from Yongping west to the sea, one hundred forty-five li to Jigezhuang, then four hundred twenty-six li to Tianjin—all hugging the shore under sail.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year (1566), Shuntian Grand Coordinator Geng Suichao surveyed the sea route: from west of Yongping to the sea it was 145 li to Jigezhuang, then 426 li to Tianjin, all navigable along the coast.

sentences.zh: 其間開洋百二十里，有建河、糧河、小沽、大沽河可避風。

translations.literal: Among this, one hundred twenty li of open sea; Jian River, Liang River, Xiaogu, and Dagou rivers could shelter from wind.
translations.idiomatic: One stretch of open sea ran 120 li; the Jian, Liang, Xiaogu, and Dagou rivers offered shelter from wind.

sentences.zh: 初允其議，尋以御史劉翾疏沮而罷。

translations.literal: At first the plan was approved; soon, on Censor Liu Xuan's memorial obstructing it, it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was approved at first, but soon abandoned after Censor Liu Xuan objected.

sentences.zh: 是年，從給事中胡應嘉言，革遮洋總。

translations.literal: That year, following Supervising Secretary Hu Yingjia's memorial, the Zheyang command was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, on Supervising Secretary Hu Yingjia's memorial, the Zheyang command was abolished.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年，徐、邳河淤，從給事中宋良佐言，復設遮洋總，存海運遺意。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing, the Xu and Pi rivers silted; following Supervising Secretary Song Liangzuo's memorial, the Zheyang command was restored, preserving the idea of sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Longqing (1571), when the Xu and Pi rivers silted up, Supervising Secretary Song Liangzuo's memorial led to the Zheyang command being restored as a vestige of sea transport.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫梁夢龍極論海運之利，言：「海道南自淮安至膠州，北自天津至海倉，島人商賈所出入。

translations.literal: Shandong Grand Coordinator Liang Menglong strongly argued the benefit of sea transport, saying: "The sea route south from Huai'an to Jiaozhou, north from Tianjin to Haicang—these are where islanders and merchants come and go.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Grand Coordinator Liang Menglong made a forceful case for sea transport: "South from Huai'an to Jiaozhou and north from Tianjin to Haicang are the lanes islanders and merchants already use.

sentences.zh: 臣遣卒自淮、膠各運米麥至天津，無不利者。

translations.literal: Your servant sent troops from Huai and Jiaozhou each to transport rice and wheat to Tianjin—without disadvantage.
translations.idiomatic: I sent men from Huai'an and Jiaozhou to ship rice and wheat to Tianjin by that route without mishap.

sentences.zh: 淮安至天津三千三百里，風便，兩旬可達。

translations.literal: Huai'an to Tianjin is three thousand three hundred li; winds favorable, in two ten-day periods it can arrive.
translations.idiomatic: From Huai'an to Tianjin is 3,300 li; with fair winds the run takes about twenty days.

sentences.zh: 舟由近洋，島嶼聯絡，雖風可依，視殷明略故道甚安便。

translations.literal: Boats by the near sea, islands linked; though wind can be relied on, compared with Yin Minglue's old route it is very safe and convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels keep to the near-shore waters where islands lie in chains; even in wind they have shelter. The course is far safer and handier than Yin Minglue's old route.

sentences.zh: 五月前風順而柔，此時出海可保無虞。

translations.literal: Before the fifth month winds are favorable and soft; at this time putting out to sea can be kept without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Before the fifth month the winds are steady and mild; sailing then is safest.

sentences.zh: 」命量撥近地漕糧十二萬石，俾夢龍行之。

translations.literal: " An order measured and allocated one hundred twenty thousand shi of nearby canal grain, enabling Menglong to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: " The court ordered 120,000 shi of nearby canal grain allocated for Menglong to move by sea.

sentences.zh: 六年，王宗沐督漕，請行海運。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Wang Zongmu supervised grain transport and asked to run sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1572), Wang Zongmu, as grain-transport commissioner, petitioned to resume sea transport.

sentences.zh: 詔令運十二萬石自淮入海。

translations.literal: An edict ordered one hundred twenty thousand shi transported from Huai'an into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered 120,000 shi shipped from Huai'an by sea.

sentences.zh: 其道，由雲梯關東北曆鷹遊山、安東衛、石臼所、夏河所、齊堂島、靈山衛、古鎮、膠州、鰲山衛、大嵩衛、行村寨，皆海面。

translations.literal: Its route—from northeast of Yunti Pass through Yingyou Hill, Andong Guard, Shijiu Station, Xiahe Station, Qitang Island, Lingshan Guard, Gu Town, Jiaozhou, Aoshan Guard, Dasong Guard, Xingjia Village—all on the sea surface.
translations.idiomatic: The route ran from northeast of Yunti Pass through Yingyou Hill, Andong Guard, Shijiu Station, Xiahe Station, Qitang Island, Lingshan Guard, Gu Town, Jiaozhou, Aoshan Guard, Dasong Guard, and Xingjia Village—all open sea.

sentences.zh: 自海洋所曆竹島、寧津所、靖海衛，東北轉成山衛、劉公島、威海衛，西曆甯海衛，皆海面。

translations.literal: From Haiyang Station through Zhudao, Ningjin Station, Jinghai Guard, turning northeast to Chengshan Guard, Liugong Island, Weihai Guard, west through Ninghai Guard—all on the sea surface.
translations.idiomatic: From Haiyang Station it passed Zhudao and Ningjin Station, Jinghai Guard, then northeast to Chengshan Guard, Liugong Island, and Weihai Guard, and west through Ninghai Guard—all on the sea.

sentences.zh: 自福山之罘島至登州城北新海口沙門等島，西曆桑島、曵母曵已島，自曵母曵已西曆三山島、芙蓉島、萊州大洋、海倉口；

translations.literal: From Fushan's Chifu Island to Dengzhou city's north new sea mouth, Shamen and other islands, west through Sang Island, Yemu and Yiyi islands; from Yemu and Yiyi west through Sanshan Island, Furong Island, Laizhou great sea, Haicang mouth;
translations.idiomatic: From Chifu Island off Fushan to the new sea mouth north of Dengzhou, with Shamen and other islands, then west past Sang Island and the Yemu and Yiyi islands; west of Yemu and Yiyi through Sanshan Island, Furong Island, the Laizhou open sea, and Haicang mouth;

sentences.zh: 自海倉西曆淮河海口、魚兒鋪，西北曆侯鎮店、唐頭塞；

translations.literal: From Haicang west through Huai River sea mouth, Yuerpu, northwest through Houzhen Shop, Tangtou Fort;
translations.idiomatic: west of Haicang through the Huai River estuary and Yuerpu, northwest through Houzhen Shop and Tangtou Fort;

sentences.zh: 自侯鎮西北大清河、小清河海口，乞溝河入直沽，抵天津衛。

translations.literal: From Houzhen northwest, Great Qing River and Little Qing River sea mouths, Qigou River entering Zhigu, reaching Tianjin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: and northwest from Houzhen through the Great and Little Qing River estuaries and the Qigou River into Zhigu, to Tianjin Guard.

sentences.zh: 凡三千三百九十里。

translations.literal: In all three thousand three hundred ninety li.
translations.idiomatic: The whole distance was 3,390 li.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，即墨福山島壞糧運七艘，漂米數千石，溺軍丁十五人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, at Jimo Fushan Island seven grain-transport ships were wrecked; several thousand shi of rice drifted; fifteen transport soldiers drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli (1573), seven grain ships were wrecked off Fushan Island in Jimo; several thousand shi of rice were lost and fifteen transport soldiers drowned.

sentences.zh: 給事、御史交章論其失，罷不復行。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors together memorialized on the failure; it was halted and not run again.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors memorialized on the disaster, and sea transport was halted and not resumed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，倭寇作，自登州運糧給朝鮮軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Japanese raiders rose; grain was transported from Dengzhou to supply the Korean campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (1597), during the Japanese invasions, grain was shipped from Dengzhou to supply the army in Korea.

sentences.zh: 山東副使於仁廉復言：「餉遼莫如海運，海運莫如登、萊。

translations.literal: Shandong Vice Commissioner Yu Renlian again said: "Supplying Liaodong is best by sea transport; sea transport is best by Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Vice Commissioner Yu Renlian argued again: "To feed Liaodong nothing beats sea transport, and for sea transport nothing beats the Dengzhou-Laizhou route.

sentences.zh: 蓋登、萊度金州六七百里，至旅順口僅五百餘里，順風揚帆一二日可至。

translations.literal: For Deng and Lai the crossing to Jinzhou is six or seven hundred li; to Lüshun mouth only five hundred-odd li—with favorable wind, sails raised, in one or two days it can arrive.
translations.idiomatic: From Dengzhou and Laizhou it is six or seven hundred li to Jinzhou and only five hundred-odd li to Lüshunkou; with a fair wind one can arrive in a day or two.

sentences.zh: 又有沙門、鼉磯、皇城等島居其中，天設水遞，止宿避風。

translations.literal: Moreover Shamen, Tuoji, Huangcheng, and other islands lie among them—Heaven set a water relay, for mooring and sheltering from wind.
translations.idiomatic: Shamen, Tuoji, Huangcheng, and other islands lie along the way—nature's own courier stations for anchorage and shelter.

sentences.zh: 惟皇城至旅順二百里差遠，得便風不半日可度也。

translations.literal: Only Huangcheng to Lüshun is two hundred li somewhat far; with convenient wind, in not half a day it can be crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Only the two hundred li from Huangcheng to Lüshun is somewhat long; with a fair wind it can be crossed in half a day.

sentences.zh: 若天津至遼，則大洋無泊；

translations.literal: If Tianjin to Liaodong, then the great ocean has no mooring;
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjin-Liaodong route, by contrast, offers no shelter on the open ocean;

sentences.zh: 淮安至膠州，雖僅三百里，而由膠至登千里而遙，礁礙難行。

translations.literal: Huai'an to Jiaozhou, though only three hundred li, yet from Jiao to Deng a thousand li and remote—reefs and obstacles hard to sail.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'an to Jiaozhou is only three hundred li, but from Jiaozhou to Dengzhou is a thousand li of reefs and difficult water;

sentences.zh: 惟登、萊濟遼，勢便而事易。

translations.literal: Only Deng and Lai to aid Liaodong—the situation convenient and the affair easy.
translations.idiomatic: only the Dengzhou-Laizhou run to supply Liaodong is both convenient and practicable.

sentences.zh: 」時頗以其議為然，而未行也。

translations.literal: " At the time many took his argument as correct, yet it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Many at court found his argument persuasive, but it was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，山東巡撫李長庚奏行海運，特設戶部侍郎一人督之，事具《長庚傳》。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, Shandong Grand Coordinator Li Changgeng memorialized to run sea transport; a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially appointed to supervise—the matter is in the "Biography of Changgeng."
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year (1618), Shandong Grand Coordinator Li Changgeng memorialized to resume sea transport; a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially appointed to oversee it—the affair is recorded in Li Changgeng's biography.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十二年，崇明人沈廷揚為內閣中書，復陳海運之便，且輯《海運書》五捲進呈。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chongzhen, Shen Tingyang of Chongming, as Secretariat drafter, again urged the convenience of sea transport, and compiled five scrolls of "Sea Transport Book" to present.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Chongzhen (1639), Shen Tingyang of Chongming, serving as a Secretariat drafter, again urged the advantages of sea transport and compiled a five-scroll Sea Transport Book for presentation.

sentences.zh: 命造海舟試之。

translations.literal: An order was given to build sea ships for trial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered sea-going vessels built for trial.

sentences.zh: 廷揚乘二舟，載米數百石，十三年六月朔，由淮安出海，望日抵天津。

translations.literal: Tingyang took two boats, loaded several hundred shi of rice; in the thirteenth year, sixth month, first day of the month, from Huai'an out to sea; on the day of full moon reached Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyang sailed two vessels loaded with several hundred shi of rice; on the first day of the sixth month of the thirteenth year (1640) he put out from Huai'an and reached Tianjin on the day of the full moon.

sentences.zh: 守風者五日，行僅一旬。

translations.literal: Waiting for wind five days; sailing only one ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: He had waited on wind for five days; the passage took only ten days.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，加廷揚戶部郎中，命往登州與巡撫徐人龍計度。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted Tingyang to Revenue Bureau Director, and ordered him to Dengzhou to plan with Grand Coordinator Xu Renlong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, promoted Tingyang to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent him to Dengzhou to plan with Grand Coordinator Xu Renlong.

sentences.zh: 山東副總兵黃廕恩亦上海運九議，帝即令督海運。

translations.literal: Shandong Vice Commander-in-chief Huang Yin'en also submitted nine proposals on sea transport; the emperor immediately ordered him to supervise sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Vice Commander Huang Yin'en also submitted nine proposals on sea transport, and the emperor at once put him in charge.

sentences.zh: 先是，寧遠軍餉率用天津船赴登州，候東南風轉粟至天津，又候西南風轉至寧遠。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ningyuan army rations mostly used Tianjin boats to go to Dengzhou, wait for southeast wind to shift grain to Tianjin, then wait for southwest wind to shift to Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, rations for the Ningyuan garrison had relied on Tianjin vessels sailing to Dengzhou, waiting for a southeast wind to carry grain to Tianjin, then a southwest wind to carry it on to Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 廷揚自登州直輸寧遠，省費多。

translations.literal: Tingyang from Dengzhou directly transported to Ningyuan, saving much expense.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyang shipped straight from Dengzhou to Ningyuan, saving considerable cost.

sentences.zh: 尋命赴淮安經理海運，為督漕侍郎硃大典所沮，乃命易駐登州，領寧遠餉務。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to go to Huai'an to manage sea transport; obstructed by Grain Transport Vice Minister Zhu Dadian, then ordered to change station to Dengzhou, overseeing Ningyuan rations.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to Huai'an to manage sea transport, but Grain Transport Vice Minister Zhu Dadian blocked him; he was then reassigned to Dengzhou to oversee Ningyuan supplies.

sentences.zh: 十六年加光祿少卿。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1643) he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 福王時，命廷揚以海舟防江，尋命兼理糧務。

translations.literal: In the Prince of Fu's time, Tingyang was ordered to defend the Yangtze with sea boats, soon also ordered to oversee grain affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was ordered to defend the Yangtze with sea vessels, and soon afterward to oversee grain affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 南都既失，廷揚崎嶇唐、魯二王間以死。

translations.literal: After the Southern Capital was lost, Tingyang wandered between the Tang and Lu princes and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing fell he moved between the Tang and Lu pretenders and died in their service.

sentences.zh: 當嘉靖中，廷臣紛紛議復海運，漕運總兵官萬表言：「在昔海運，歲溺不止十萬。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period, courtiers repeatedly debated restoring sea transport; grain-transport Commander Wan Biao said: "In former times under sea transport, yearly drowning was not less than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign courtiers repeatedly debated restoring sea transport. Grain-transport Commander Wan Biao warned: "Under the old sea transport, yearly losses to drowning alone ran to a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 載米之舟，駕船之卒，統卒之官，皆所不免。

translations.literal: Grain-carrying boats, boat-steering troops, and the officers commanding the troops—all were unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: Boats, boatmen, and the officers commanding them—all perished without exception.

sentences.zh: 今人策海運輒主丘浚之論，非達於事者也。」

translations.literal: Today when people plan sea transport they always take Qiu Jun's theory as master—not those who grasp affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Those who urge sea transport today always invoke Qiu Jun's arguments; they are not men who understand how things actually work."
